# Committed dense trajectory corpus

Search snapshot: `a4582b9f2d02198cfbe0ac6f85f3db058402b1bc`.
Read-only searches covered `motion-server/`, `weld_planner/` and
`offline-programming/`, including tracked binaries, fixtures and encoder callers.
There is **one distinct committed .rdt file and zero real planner outputs**.
The file below is a synthetic cross-language codec reference; it is not evidence
of an actual planned weld. No programs have been fabricated to fill the corpus.

| File | Origin path | Last modifying commit | Producer | Bytes |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| dense_joint_trajectory_reference.rdt | motion-server/v2/testdata/dense_joint_trajectory_reference.rdt | a3bcb8258f4667b4aa4bee3c40886cef7031fbfe | motion-server/v2/tools/make_reference_fixture.py, using weld_planner/v1/python/weld_programmer/export/dense_joint_trajectory.py | 2796 |

`motion-server/v2/tools/make_reference_fixture.py` documents a deterministic
stdlib-only command, but writes into the producer tree. Its committed output was
copied verbatim because that tree is read-only for this task.
`motion-server/v2/tools/bench_play.py` creates synthetic trajectories in memory
and uploads them to the joint trajectory daemon. Its documented command requires
the mujoco-sim Pixi environment and installed joint trajectory daemon and velocity
controller binaries; it is not a standalone hermetic export command.
The weld planner encoder tests create synthetic in-memory fixtures. No other
committed `.rdt` outputs or documented hermetic real-planner export command were
found. The existing reference requests torch I/O, which native Start must refuse
until the process executor is qualified.

`REPORT.json` is generated by `go run ./tools/rdtcheck -json
adapters/rosie/densejointtraj/testdata/corpus/REPORT.json` from the rt-core directory.
`TestCorpusReportIsCurrent` regenerates it in memory and compares exact bytes.
A6 count conversion and native limits come from the bench configuration; the
single bench axis is repeated in source J1..J9 order for analysis, not represented
as a deployed nine-axis machine. Local clock reset gaps and assembled gaps are
reported separately. Normalised counts describe the seam policy even when the
bench's native limits reject the reference program.
